Subject: Promo packaging question — Spark Accelerator pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers looked great. We're finalizing our accelerator benefits packet and have two asks that would make Redwood an easy yes from our selection committee: 1) increase the pilot credits to $25k (from the standard $10k) to cover larger model experiments, and 2) allow us to pair that pilot credit with an introductory reserved-capacity discount (20% off committed monthly spend for the first 6 months) so we can move faster into a production spike if experiments look good.

We know that combining credits + commit discounts isn't the default. Can you share whether Redwood can make a one-off packaging exception for Spark cohort partners? We can commit to a 6-month pilot term and share a short usage projection (attached). If legal/ops need a term sheet, happy to sign an MSA addendum.

Attachments: "pricing-model.xlsx" (spreadsheet)

Best,
Elena
Director, Spark Accelerator
BrightSeed Inc.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Promo packaging question — Spark Accelerator pilot

Hi Elena — really appreciate the clear ask and the usage file. Ben/Marissa are looped in so we can evaluate from pricing and partner ops. Quick answers up front:

- $25k pilot credit is large but not impossible for flagship accelerator partners — we typically need approvals above $15k.
- Combining a pilot credit + a short-term reserved discount is something we can offer via a limited addendum (we've done similar for a few strategic cohorts), but we need to pin the commit floor and the product shape (hosted API vs. early dedicated).

To move quickly, can you confirm: 1) whether BrightSeed expects to run mostly hosted API workloads (short lived) vs. sustained dedicated inference, and 2) an estimated peak concurrent tokens per minute for the pilot month? That will help us size a realistic reserved commit and quantify the risk.

I'll attach a short term sheet draft for a packaging exception (internal draft) and loop Irene from legal to speed sign-off if we land numbers.

Thanks — talk soon,
Soojin
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: "SparkAccelerator_TermSheet_v3.pdf" (term sheet stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Promo packaging question — Spark Accelerator pilot

Soojin / Marissa — quick internal analysis after reviewing Elena's projection:

Summary proposal we can take to Ops/Finance for a one-off exception:

- Pilot credits: $20,000 prepaid consumption credit (we can stretch to $25k but require exec approval).
- Reserved discount: 18% off for the first 6 months on a minimum committed spend of $6,000/month (billed monthly).
- Conversion clause: any unused pilot credit converts to a one-time invoice credit toward the first reserved invoice within 90 days.
- Usage guardrail: we require a 30-day lookback telemetry export during the pilot and a simple spike cap (overage rate at our standard pay-as-you-go price).
- Time to sign: if BrightSeed agrees, we can get a short addendum signed within 5 business days; Irene flagged two small legal clarifications (export controls + data retention alignment) that are standard.

Rationale: $25k *and* full 20% off would be too favorable for a first pass. This split ($20k + 18% on $6k/mo) preserves upside for BrightSeed while protecting Redwood's capacity economics. If Soojin wants to push to $25k we need a Sales Exec/Revenue Ops approval.

Next steps: If Marissa confirms ops feasibility, Soojin can send updated term sheet and I'll prepare a concise internal approval note for RevOps.

-Ben
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what the committee will accept. Two small asks before we sign: 1) can the reserved commit minimum be phrased as a monthly "soft" commit (i.e., allow one month per quarter to dip 50% without penalty) so our student teams with lumpy demos don't get stuck, and 2) the conversion of unused credits — could you allow a 120-day window instead of 90? Those two tweaks make internal finance comfortable.

If Redwood can accept those two changes, BrightSeed is prepared to sign the addendum and schedule a kick-off within 10 business days. I've attached a short internal approval note so you can see the committee language (not public).
